blocks.li: Every bench on one scale: 0 = random guessing, 100 = perfect; higher is better ↑.

Turkish Reading (656 questions) and Turkish Grammar (1,542), 5 options each, English Reading (547 of the reading questions translated into English, 5 options) and Logic and Math: accuracy corrected for chance, (accuracy − 1/k) / (1 − 1/k) × 100, k the number of options. Vision: the same on Reading's 763 questions that depend on the printed page, read from the page image alone.
Backgammon: 0 = the error rate of a player that picks a random legal move, 100 = no error.

Answer Check (2,069 pairs of a machine-written English summary, a question and its reference answer; 3 labels: the summary states that answer, a conflicting one or none): the same correction with k = 3; its reference labels come from two model judges, not people (how it was built).

Combined = the plain mean of Reading · Turkish (all 2,198 Turkish questions), Logic & Math (pooled) and Backgammon, equal weights, as before the splits, only for a model that ran all three, one model on every bench (the rule).
Decision Index = the plain mean of English Reading, Logic, Math and Answer Check, equal weights, only for a model on all four, one model on every bench, as for Combined (the rule).

Each bar is a model's score in its maker's colour, the maker's mark before its name; the small tag beside the name says how the setup ran where its file gives one (setting · route · snapshot), then the training method where our records state it. A bar, like a dot on the charts, opens the model's page. Jev 1.14 is the reference bar: TypeSafe's hosted Jev 1.14, the model the index's entries reproduce: a reference bar, with no index score of its own here.
Class: the Reading site's Leaderboard's, by total parameters, else by list price (the classes).
Learning from experience ("did it improve?", points gained, higher is better ↑) is a column of its own, outside the combined score.
Lower is better ↓ for calibration error (ECE, in points: how far the stated probabilities are from the hit rate) and latency. Close scores read tied, never with an interval: the rule.

The table under the chart: Not run, the model is not on that bench; Not applicable, the score does not apply (Combined without all three groups), the reason on hover or focus. Rank is the place by the chosen score among the models in view, 1, 2, 3 without repeats; models with the same score keep the table's order, which claims no difference (no bench's file carries an all-pairs test, so no tiers). A column head sorts by it; again, the other way.

Full results adds under each score its calibration error (ECE, points), learning from experience and latency: Reading · Turkish requests on one pinned machine (spark2, a DGX Spark (GB10)), one request at a time, median and 95th percentile.
